followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain one Ras Jedir protest campaign with two separated operational observations. Reported repeated openings prevent one continuous campaign-length closure. Preserve December emergency and returning-Libyan exceptions, and January ambulance/emergency exceptions. Checkpoint restrictions and Ben Guerdane approach obstruction remain distinguishable. Keep P1 onset 13 December and last confirmation 14 December 2016, minimum one calendar day with unknown endpoint. Keep P2 unknown onset, closure confirmed 22 January and actual return 23 January 2017, with no numeric duration. The 17 January deal is not a reopening. Retain both Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests and Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs, services and livelihoods as reported demands, without an exclusive causal ranking. Webdo’s December article relays TAP; unavailable DirectInfo is not extra evidence. Libya Herald supplies January traffic and attributed sources; Webdo’s 12 January article supports repeated interruptions, not a precise final-spell onset. Retain both phases unlocated at Ras Jedir and the Ben Guerdane approach, with null coordinates. No shared continuous December-to-January map interval is justified.
